acceptance: A `/oracle-review` comment, or a thread reply, can request a fresh review of the same head, bounded so it cannot loop
The reviewer brief includes unresolved thread replies and asks the reviewer to confirm or withdraw each disputed finding with a reason
Regression fixture: a disputed finding with author evidence on the same head is re-judged, not skipped
At most 2 forced rounds per head; a third request is refused with a message (test)
Withdrawals must carry citations verified by mark_citations and never auto-resolve threads
Replay fixture of #3222: a docs-only rebuttal on the same head is re-judged, not carried
context: In PR #3233 (branch fix/oracle-same-head-rerereview). Trigger narrowed for security: the oracle found that a pull_request_review_comment trigger runs PR-controlled workflow code with secrets, so thread replies no longer start a round; rebuttals arrive via /oracle-review comments (default-branch context) and pushes, and a push that leaves a thread disputed upgrades to a forced follow-up. Forced rounds only after SHIP/SHIP WITH FIXES, at most 2 per head; withdrawals need a citation in files_examined that resolves to a head line; no auto-resolve.
description: On #3092 the oracle (muse) raised "Schema-qualified CLUSTER uses unqualified index name" (thread 4302987072) and kept it open on head 9d7b7a148 and head 397a4b3f3. PostgreSQL's `CLUSTER table USING index_name` accepts only an unqualified index name; the qualified form failed live on PostgreSQL 17 with `syntax error at or near "."`. A reply with that evidence plus a `/oracle-review` comment did not trigger a re-review: the verdict plan skipped with "head 9d7b7a148... already has a failure result" (_project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/retry.py:84; protocol.py:263). The only way forward was another commit. The next review then reported "New tests explicitly assert the D2 buggy SQL", and only a rebase and another head got SHIP, which called the finding "not a correctness defect". The PR needed an owner decision in between. There are two gaps: (1) no same-head re-review after an author rebuttal; (2) the reviewer brief does not ask the reviewer to weigh thread replies or check the claimed SQL grammar.
